classicasp.notes:
REALITY: classic ASP is a legacy stack, so there is NO giant single-stack corpus. Real, de-duplicated classic/aspnet-mixed material tops out around ~250k-300k lines; everything above that is synthetic permutation. The generator should (a) download the real sources, (b) extension-filter the mixed Assetnote/random-robbie files to .asp/.asa/.inc lines for the classicasp bucket (share .aspx/.ashx/.asmx/.svc with an aspnet bucket), then (c) permute.

T1 ~200k (ESSENTIALLY ALL REAL): concat Assetnote combined asp/aspx family (~95k) + random-robbie asp.txt (~21k) + aspx.txt (~90k) + ashx.txt (~27k) + SecLists IIS/FrontPage/SVNDigger + fuzzdb + these seeds, then dedup. Lands ~200k-280k real lines. Optionally add one light backup pass (×{.bak,.old}) only if short. ~95-100% real.

T2 ~1M (~25% real / ~75% synthetic): take base = (real classicasp filenames with extension stripped) ∪ raft-large-words (~120k) ∪ first ~200k of Assetnote httparchive_directories_1m → ~350k unique bases. Cross with core classic-ASP extensions {asp, asa, inc, cdx, cer, htr, stm, shtml} (8) → ~2.8M raw; dedup + cap to 1M. Alternative quick-fill: append Assetnote directories_1m wholesale, but that is generic (lower hit-rate) — prefer base×ext.

T3 ~3M (~10% real / ~90% synthetic): base (~350k) × ext (8) × backup-suffix {"", .bak, .old, .txt, "~", .save, .orig} plus the iconic source-disclosure variants (::$DATA, +.htr) applied to top ~2k bases; add random-robbie combined_directories.txt (~640k) and DirBuster-2.3-big (~1.27M) crossed with .asp. Cap/dedup to 3M. Flag: beyond ~300k nothing is real classic-ASP — T2/T3 are permutation-reached, and because live classic-ASP targets are small, huge tiers mainly serve exhaustive offline fuzzing, not realistic hit-rate.

HIGH-CONFIDENCE classifier discriminators (won't mis-bucket): asp, asa, cdx, htr, idc, idq, ida, global.asa, _vti_bin, _vti_pvt, iisadmpwd, msadc(s.dll), adovbs.inc, ewebeditor, dispbbs.asp, dvbbs, bbsxp, zb_system, iisstart.asp. SHARED/weaker tokens (may also hit PHP/Apache/.NET, keep but score lower): inc, cer, stm, shtm, shtml, mdb, web.config, fckeditor, ashx/asmx/svc.

LICENSING: SecLists = MIT (permissive). Assetnote wordlists = Apache-2.0 (ship NOTICE/attribution; the httparchive lists are derived from public crawl data). random-robbie/bruteforce-lists = LICENSE present (~Apache-2.0 size) — verify before shipping. fuzzdb = mixed/CC-BY-SA-style — attribution required; SVNDigger subset carries its own Licence. All are redistributable for a bundled offline generator provided attribution/NOTICE files are preserved.

coldfusion.notes:
REAL vs SYNTHETIC for ColdFusion/CFML. Truly CF-classified real paths are scarce: curated framework lists (SecLists ColdFusion.fuzz 203 + fuzzdb ColdFusion 111 + JRun 13 + login/cfm 294 + SVNDigger 25) plus these ~290 seeds dedupe to roughly 900-1,100 unique framework/secret/scaffold paths - these are exactly what generic corpora MISS (grepping Assetnote's 71.6k cfm corpus for CFIDE/lucee/railo/adminapi returned ZERO; only cfusion.cfm appeared). Real .cfm page-name volume comes from Assetnote cfm-series (71.6k mixed, realistically ~10-20k truly cfm after classifying) + random-robbie cfm.txt (1,006), i.e. ~15-25k real .cfm paths. So pure-real CF ~= 20-30k lines; the dedicated-stack corpus is far below any tier on its own.

HOW TO HIT THE TIERS:
T1 ~200k (~45% real / ~55% permutation): union all real (the ~1k framework seeds + full Assetnote cfm-series 71.6k used wholesale + jsp-series 19.5k folded in + random-robbie 1k) ~= ~90k real bases; then extension-swap each base across {cfm, cfml, cfc, dbm} (x4) and keep directory forms -> ~200k+.
T2 ~1M (~15-20% real / ~80% synthetic): take ~50k unique bases x {cfm,cfml,cfc,dbm} (=200k) x backup-suffix set {"", .bak, .old, ~, .orig, .save} (x6) ~= ~1M. Equivalent: append a CF-token-classified slice of Assetnote httparchive_directories_1m.
T3 ~3M (>90% synthetic): expand backup suffixes (.bak .old .orig .save .swp .tmp .inc .1 .2 _bak .copy .txt .cfm.bak + archive forms .zip/.tar.gz of dirs), add case permutations (CFIDE<->cfide, .cfm<->.CFM), and cross-fold a big GENERIC directory substrate (SecLists directory-list-2.3-big ~1.2M and/or Assetnote directories_1m) salted with CF prefixes/tokens. At 3M the list is effectively a generic dir corpus seeded with CF markers, not a CF-unique corpus - flag it to the operator as low-precision.

BACKUP-PRONE BASES to drive base x ext x backup permutation: the neo-*.xml config set, password.properties/seed.properties, lucee-server.xml / lucee-web.xml.cfm, railo-*.xml.cfm, bluedragon.xml, box.json/server.json/.cfconfig.json, Application.cfc/Application.cfm. These rarely appear in generic corpora and are the highest-value permutation seeds.

CLASSIFIER CAUTION: keep jsp/jspx OUT of the primary CF extension set (they belong to a java/jsp bucket) - rely on CF-specific path tokens (cfide, adminapi, flex2gateway, jrunscripts, cfusion, lucee, railo-context, cf_scripts) so the CF bucket stays precise. Dropped cf-templates as a token (collides with AWS CloudFormation S3 buckets) and server.json as a token (too generic; kept only as a seed path).

LICENSING: SecLists = MIT; nuclei-templates = MIT; fuzzdb = Creative Commons / copyfree (attribution expected - verify LICENSE); Assetnote wordlists = freely downloadable/redistributable (verify assetnote/wordlists repo license, historically permissive); random-robbie/bruteforce-lists = check repo LICENSE before shipping. All paths themselves are non-copyrightable facts; attribution of the source lists in the generator's credits is the safe practice. Assetnote files regenerate monthly (28th, or 27th in 2025-2026) - the generator should resolve the latest date from the /data/automated/ and /data/technologies/ Apache directory indexes rather than pinning 2026_08_27.

dotnet.notes:
REAL .NET-specific downloadable corpus (deduped union) tops out around ~250-300k lines — there is no multi-million real .NET wordlist in existence, so T2/T3 are permutation-driven. Measured line counts (wc -l): Assetnote httparchive aspx latest (2026_08_27)=71,623 with 48 monthly snapshots whose union (high overlap) is ~300-450k unique; random-robbie aspx=70,851, dll=77,156, asp=20,239, ashx=19,252, asmx=2,040, svc=1,672, cs=4,678, old=9,897; SecLists .NET CMS (kentico/dnn/umbraco/sharepoint/sitefinity/sitecore) ~40-60k combined; fuzzdb IIS/ADFS/SharePoint/FrontPage ~3-4k.

T1 (~200k): essentially ALL REAL. Union {all recent Assetnote monthly aspx snapshots} + {random-robbie aspx/asp/ashx/asmx/svc/cs/old/dll} + {SecLists .NET CMS} + {fuzzdb dotnet} dedupes to ~200-280k. Only light synthesis needed: add the config-backup variants of web.config / appsettings.json / global.asax (a few hundred lines). ~90% real / ~10% synthetic.

T2 (~1M): real ceiling ~300k, so ~700k must be synthetic. Strip extensions from the real union to get ~120-150k unique base names, then cross-multiply by the .NET extension set {.aspx .asp .asmx .ashx .svc .axd .config .ascx .master .cshtml .asax} (11) → ~1.3-1.6M, dedupe/cap to 1M. Equivalent path: real(~300k) + backup-suffix permutation {.bak .old .orig .save .txt .tmp ~ .1 .copy .disabled .inc .back} applied to every config/source base. ~30% real / ~70% synthetic.

T3 (~3M): ~90%+ synthetic. Cleanest: take a generic directory/word base (SecLists DirBuster-2007_directory-list-2.3-big = 1,273,832 lines, or Assetnote directories_1m ~1M, or raft-large-words 119,600) and append >=3-4 .NET extensions to each (1.27M x 4 = 5.1M) then dedupe/cap to 3M, keeping only lines the classifier buckets as dotnet. Alternatively T2-union(~1M) x {case-variants + 2-3 backup suffixes}. NOTE on case: IIS/ASP.NET paths are case-insensitive, so lowercasing collapses duplicates safely for actual scanning — but KEEPING case variants (Default.aspx vs default.aspx) is a cheap, legitimate permutation specifically useful to inflate toward a tier when you want raw count.

general.notes: TIERING (real corpora, deduped, no leading slash). T1 ~200k 'fast': union of the curated seed_lines + SecLists quickhits.txt + Bo0oM fuzz.txt + dirsearch dicc.txt(%EXT% expanded) + common.txt + raft-large-{directories,files,words} (mixed-case). After casefold-dedup that lands ~170-200k; top up to 200k with DirBuster medium (which alone is 220,560 - a clean single-source T1 fallback). T2 ~1M 'deep': T1 UNION assetnote httparchive_directories_1m (696,827, resolve current dated file via automated.json) UNION DirBuster-2007_directory-list-2.3-medium (220,560) UNION big.txt/combined_directories -> dedup ~0.9-1.0M. T3 ~3M 'full': T2 UNION DirBuster-2007_directory-list-2.3-big (1,273,833) UNION assetnote wordlist_no_underscores (1.9M) [optionally wordlist_with_underscores 2.67M / OneListForAll onelistforallshort 2.5M] -> dedup ~3M real. REAL vs PERMUTATION: the counts above are REAL union lines. To inflate toward a target without adding corpora, PERMUTE top-N names x the extensions[] backup/archive suffixes (e.g. top ~20k names x ~45 suffixes = ~900k synthetic candidates like config.bak, admin.zip, db.sql.gz); permuted entries are lower-signal, so generate them as a trailing section AFTER the real union and cap per-name (e.g. 6-8 suffixes on the top 5k names) rather than full cartesian. DEDUP/CASE: normalize = trim whitespace, strip leading/trailing '/', drop blank lines and comment lines (#, !, ;), drop entries containing scheme://, '?', '#', or spaces, NFC. CASE: Linux paths are case-sensitive so Admin != admin matters - keep the mixed-case union as the canonical 'full' set; ALSO emit a casefold-deduped (lowercase) variant for case-insensitive targets and for the smaller tiers (raft ships -lowercase variants ready for this). Dedup case-SENSITIVELY for T3, case-INSENSITIVELY for T1/T2 to keep them tight. LICENSING CAVEATS for a redistributed combined list: SecLists MIT, Bo0oM WTFPL, Assetnote Apache-2.0, trickest MIT all permit redistribution with attribution (ship a SOURCES.md crediting each). dirsearch dicc.txt is GPL-2.0 (copyleft) and OneListForAll has NO license - keep BOTH as runtime-fetched scan inputs or clearly-segregated optional pulls rather than baking their lines into a permissively-relicensed shipped blob. Prefer pulling at install/build time from the raw/CDN URLs over vendoring, so the public repo stays small and licenses stay with the source.

java.notes:
REAL Java-specific corpus is unusually large for this stack thanks to Assetnote's manual per-extension lists, so tiers lean more on real data than most stacks.

T1 (~200k) - REACHABLE WITH REAL DATA, little/no permutation: Assetnote manual do.txt (~160k .do/Struts/Spring-MVC) + jsp.txt (~90k JSP), deduped ~=180-220k; top up with httparchive_jsp_jspa_do_action (~12k), SecLists raft-large-directories (~62k) and the curated framework seeds/fuzzdb/SecLists/random-robbie files (~3-5k). Clean, high-signal.

T2 (~1M): unique REAL Java-specific content plateaus around ~250-300k (do.txt + jsp.txt + httparchive + framework files heavily overlap). Reach 1M by (a) folding in generic-but-applicable big corpora the classifier buckets into Java -- httparchive_directories_1m (~1M), httparchive_apiroutes (~400k, great for Spring REST), SecLists DirBuster directory-list-2.3-big (~1.2M), raft-large-words (~90k); and/or (b) light permutation: ~90k raft-large-words bases x Java extensions {jsp,jspx,jspf,do,action,faces,jsf,xhtml} ~= 720k. T3 (~3M): dominated by synthetic permutation + generic corpora. nodejs.notes: TIER MATH (this stack). The Node-SPECIFIC real corpus is actually modest: the only high-precision real lists are Assetnote httparchive_express (147k), SecLists api/* (~40k), random-robbie curated (a few k), and the ~330 curated seeds. The big volume comes from generic-but-on-format corpora bucketed by extension (.js/.json/.ts/.map/.env). T1 ~200k (REAL): httparchive_express (147k) + SecLists api/* (~40k) + raft-large-words (120k) + seeds, dedup -> ~200k, essentially 100% real; OR a token-filtered slice of httparchive_js (lines with _next/_nuxt/dist/build/static/js/chunk/bundle/webpack/assets) which yields ~150-300k real. T2 ~1M (REAL, no synthetic needed): httparchive_js (3.99M raw, or token-filtered) + httparchive_apiroutes (403k) + httparchive_directories_1m (697k) + dot_filenames filtered to node dotfiles (.env/.npmrc/.babelrc/.eslintrc/.prettierrc/.nvmrc...), dedup -> comfortably 1M+. T3 ~3M: httparchive_js alone is 3.99M raw and dedups/normalizes to ~3M REAL; combine with dot_filenames (3.19M) and raw dedup clears 3M with margin. So for THIS stack T3 is reachable from REAL corpus purely on the strength of the js + dotfile lists - permutation is NOT required for volume. CAVEAT on precision vs volume: that volume is generic .js/dotfile paths bucketed by extension, not Node-framework-unique. If you want T2/T3 with HIGH Node-framework precision (not just .js volume), you must ADD a synthetic permutation layer because no 1M+ Node-framework-unique corpus exists: take the ~330 curated base names (config/secret/entry/manifest) x extension variants {.js,.mjs,.cjs,.ts,.json,.env,.map} x backup-suffixes {.bak,.old,.save,.orig,.swp,~,.1,.2,.copy,.tmp,.gz,.zip,.tar.gz} -> ~330 x 7 x 13 = ~30k high-signal synthetic; widen base pool with raft-large-words x the same matrix to add 100k-1M+ synthetic. Net: real corpus dominates raw tiers (js + dotfiles), permutation dominates framework-precision. IMPLEMENTATION: resolve Assetnote filenames via the .json catalogs at runtime (the YYYY_MM_DD suffix rotates monthly and old URLs 404). LICENSING (all permissive, redistribution OK): SecLists MIT, nuclei-templates MIT, Assetnote wordlists Apache-2.0, random-robbie bruteforce-lists Apache-2.0, fuzzdb BSD-3-Clause. No copyleft anywhere. Apache-2.0 -> preserve attribution/NOTICE; BSD-3 -> retain fuzzdb copyright + no-endorsement clause; MIT -> include license text. perl.notes:
CORPUS REALITY: Perl/CGI has a SMALL real-world footprint and it is shrinking (legacy stack). Hard proof from Assetnote's own HTTP Archive extraction: the php list is 3.28 MB (~1M+ real paths) while cgi_pl is only 345 KB / 11,350 lines - roughly 30x smaller. After merging + dedupe + payload-stripping across Assetnote cgi_pl (~11k), SecLists CGIs/XPlatform/Microsoft (~7.4k raw -> ~3-4k unique base paths), fuzzdb CGI_* (overlaps SecLists), random-robbie perl/cgi (~2.5k), Nikto base paths (~2-3k unique after collapsing payload variants), SVNDigger pl (135) and the curated seed_lines (~380), the TRUE unique Perl-specific corpus is only ~25-35k lines. Everything above that is synthetic permutation.

HOW TO HIT THE TIERS:
- T1 ~200k: ~30k real corpus + permutation. Take ~35-40k base tokens (raft-medium/large-words or the distinct basenames already in the real corpus + common app dirs) x the core Perl ext set {pl, cgi, pm, psgi, fcgi} ~= 175k, add the 30k real = ~205k. => ~15% real, ~85% permutation.
- T2 ~1M: pure permutation. ~200k base words (raft-large-words 120k + top ~80k of Assetnote directories_1m) x 5 Perl exts {pl,cgi,pm,psgi,fcgi} = 1M. => ~97% permutation.
- T3 ~3M: pure permutation. Either 200k bases x 5 exts x 3 backup-suffixes {.bak, ~, .old} ~= 3M, or 600k bases (top of Assetnote directories_1m) x 5 exts = 3M. => ~99% permutation.
Backup-suffix set to permute (esp. against config/secret basenames localconfig, mt-config.cgi, Kernel/Config.pm, RT_SiteConfig.pm, koha-conf.xml, config.pl): .bak ~ .old .orig .save .swp .tmp .copy .1 .2 .txt .dist .sample .inc .default .-original. Also WAF/parser-bypass ext variants from fuzzdb alt-extensions-perl.txt (%00, trailing dots, case flips) for a dedicated bypass mode. Note: .cgi is the strongest Perl signal but is language-agnostic at the HTTP layer (a .cgi can be C/sh/python); bucket by .pl/.pm/.psgi/.fcgi first, treat .cgi as Perl-probable. tt/tt2/tmpl/mhtml/mas/ep/epl are template exts that strongly imply Perl but are not 100% exclusive (Template-Toolkit has ports) - keep but weight lower in the classifier.

LICENSING CAVEATS: Assetnote (Apache-2.0), SecLists (MIT), random-robbie (Apache-2.0), nuclei-templates (MIT) are all safe to download and redistribute with attribution. fuzzdb is CC BY 3.0 and bundles Skipfish dictionaries -> attribution required; since fuzzdb's CGI lists are the upstream of SecLists' copies, prefer ingesting the MIT SecLists mirror to simplify licensing. Nikto db_tests is the single exception: its header forbids use/redistribution outside the full Nikto package - do NOT bake it into the shipped corpus; mine it only for manual seed ideas or shell out to Nikto at scan time. OneListForAll aggregates many upstreams with mixed licenses - treat as feedstock only and verify before shipping."

REALITY CHECK (this stack is unusual): Python web frameworks ROUTE URLs (regex/decorator dispatch) instead of mapping files to disk, so there is essentially NO large, high-quality, Python-framework-specific PATH corpus in the public ecosystem, and Assetnote has NO .py extension list (confirmed: automated.json has php/aspx/jsp/cgi_pl but no py). Verified traps: (1) Assetnote technologies/httparchive_django.txt and _flask.txt are HOST-MAPPING lists (lists of sites running the tech), NOT path wordlists - must be excluded from the generator. (2) OLFA flask_long.txt (652 B) is mostly Flask CONFIG KEY names (SECRET_KEY, SESSION_COOKIE_*), not paths; python_long.txt is small and polluted. NET: the real Python-SPECIFIC unique path content caps at roughly 50-100k lines (OLFA django_long ~39k + swagger/graphql/api-doc specifics + the ~320 curated seeds here). Everything bigger is generic web-path corpus that the per-language classifier buckets, plus synthetic permutation. The curated seed_lines + the backup-suffix permutation engine are therefore the primary Python value-add, not downloaded corpora.

TIER STRATEGY:
- T1 ~200k (mostly REAL): curated seeds (~320) + OLFA django_long (~39k) + OLFA swagger_short + graphql_short + SecLists api/* + Assetnote apiroutes top-slice (~150k) OR SecLists raft-large-directories(62k)+raft-large-files(37k)+raft-large-words(38k)+common(4.7k)+dirsearch dicc(11k). ~90% real corpus; ~10% permutation (base x {'',.bak,.old,.orig,~,.swp} over the Python base set). - T2 ~1M (REAL, generic-dominated): Assetnote directories_1m (696,827) + apiroutes (403,119) deduped to ~1.0-1.05M; OR a single OLFA paths_long (~1.5-2M) / api_long (~2.3-3M) truncated. Only a thin slice is Python-specific; the rest is generic buckets.

ruby.notes:
CORE REALITY: Unlike PHP/ASP.NET/Java, Ruby/Rails has essentially NO large public *path* wordlist. The file everyone assumes is one - Assetnote's httparchive_rails (6.8 MB) - is a technology->host mapping (217,262 hostnames, verified 0 non-URL lines), not paths. Genuinely Ruby-distinctive PATH content available publicly is tiny: SecLists ror.txt (~190) + the seed_lines here (~330) + HackTricks CVE/traversal paths (~15) = ~500 curated lines, plus maybe ~10-30k more mined by the classifier from the Ruby-token/ext slice of the big generic corpora (directories_1m, raft, OneListForAll, combined_directories). Everything beyond ~20-30k is synthetic permutation or generic spillover. This is also inherent to Rails: real structure hides behind RESTful controller#action routes that are app-specific and not brute-forceable from a generic list - so the highest-value Ruby targets are the FIXED framework/config/secret files and the mounted gem dashboards (which seed_lines fully covers), not deep path enumeration.

HITTING THE TIERS (real corpus vs synthetic permutation):
- T1 ~200k: ~500 curated (always-include) + ~10-30k Ruby-matched lines mined by the classifier from directories_1m (697k) + raft-* + OneListForAll-micro + combined_directories. Close the gap with permutation: distinct Ruby base names B (~4-8k from seeds + mined bases) x Ruby extensions E(~15: rb,erb,haml,slim,jbuilder,rabl,builder,rake,ru,yml,...) x a plain+backup multiplier. B(6k) x E(15) = 90k; add one backup-suffix round (Common-DB-Backups templates, x~2) => ~180k. So T1 = ~20-30k real/mined + ~170k synthetic. MOSTLY SYNTHETIC.
- T2 ~1M: add the directory-prefix cross-product. ~25 canonical Rails dir prefixes (config/, config/initializers/, config/environments/, config/credentials/, app/controllers/, app/models/, app/views/, app/helpers/, app/jobs/, app/mailers/, app/channels/, db/, db/migrate/, lib/, lib/tasks/, spec/, test/, public/, public/assets/, public/packs/, storage/, log/, tmp/, vendor/) x B(6-8k) x ~5 exts ~= 750k-1M, unioned with the T1 set. Real content stays ~20-30k; ~97% synthetic.
- T3 ~3M: union the full generic aggregate as a Ruby-flavored superset - onelistforallshort (~2.5-3M) + DirBuster-big (~1.27M) + directories_1m (697k) + combined_directories (~1M), deduped to ~3-4M - then run the full Ruby permutation matrix on top (base x ext x backup x dir-prefix x {plain, leading-dot, trailing-slash, case}). 3M is reached by permutation explosion + generic spillover; genuinely Ruby-distinctive content remains a few tens of thousands at most, so per-request precision is low while coverage is maximal. ONLY permutation (and the generic kitchen-sink) can reach T3 for this stack - there is no 3M real Ruby corpus.
